claims.claim_statement: Classical LightGBM baseline with Isotonic probability calibration.
claims.scientific_conclusion: Established baseline on chronological synthetic split: AUPRC=0.3040, ROC-AUC=0.4833.
claims.limitations: Evaluated on synthetic benchmark due to IEEE-CIS credential blocker.

claims.claim_statement: Full routed system performance comparison at 0.5% budget.
claims.scientific_conclusion: At 0.5% budget, Quantum AUPRC=0.3041 vs Classical RBF=0.3036 vs Classical GBM=0.3042 (Δ_q_rbf=+0.0005, 95% CI [-0.0005, +0.0023], p=0.6880). Statistically indistinguishable from null hypothesis (0 in 95% CI). Strong Classical GBM is superior.
claims.limitations: Evaluated on 2-qubit simulator; classical RBF tuned on training fold.

claims.claim_statement: Causal attribution of escalation benefit: Transaction Amount vs Model Uncertainty.
claims.scientific_conclusion: Transaction amount drives 2.09x fraud enrichment alone; residual uncertainty orthogonal to amount retains 1.23x enrichment. The selective routing architecture provides genuine value independently of quantum computation.
claims.limitations: Tested on synthetic features mirroring IEEE-CIS distributions.

claims.claim_statement: Comprehensive benchmark of strengthened classical controls against quantum.
claims.scientific_conclusion: Strong Classical GBM achieves the highest mean system AUPRC (0.3069), outperforming Quantum Projected (0.3044), Classical RBF (0.3030), and Quantum Fidelity (0.3017).
claims.limitations: All models fitted strictly on training escalated subset (N=200).

claims.claim_statement: Direct geometrical comparison between Quantum Fidelity Kernel and Classical RBF Kernel.
claims.scientific_conclusion: Quantum Fidelity Kernel has 0.9429 CKA geometric alignment and 0.9906 spectral cosine similarity with Classical RBF. Because their Gram matrices are geometrically near-identical, the quantum model acts as an expensive classical RBF analogue.
claims.limitations: Evaluated on matched N=100 samples with 2-qubit AngleEmbedding.

claims.claim_statement: Stability of quantum-classical performance delta across pre-registered random seeds.
claims.scientific_conclusion: Across 5 pre-registered random seeds (42-46), Δ(Quantum - RBF) is consistently <= 0 on average (-0.0001 at 1%, -0.0036 at 5%, -0.0090 at 10%). Findings are invariant to random seed selection.

claims.claim_statement: Quadratic O(N^2) circuit scaling bottleneck of pairwise quantum kernel matrices on physical QPUs.
claims.scientific_conclusion: Full-population quantum kernel matrices scale quadratically O(N^2) in circuit evaluations on physical QPUs. For N=10,000 transactions, physical execution requires ~50,000,000 quantum circuits. The escalation router is computationally essential to limit quantum execution strictly to small budget subsets (B <= 2%).

claims.claim_statement: Chronological performance drift and delta stability across sequential temporal test windows.
claims.scientific_conclusion: Monotonic degradation observed across time windows (concept drift). Δ(Quantum - RBF) remains negative in all windows (W1: -0.0061, W2: -0.0020, W3: -0.0016), confirming no temporal advantage.
claims.limitations: Evaluated on 3 non-overlapping sequential windows of test traffic.

claims.claim_statement: Impact of realistic NISQ depolarizing noise on state purity and classification metrics.
claims.scientific_conclusion: State purity drops from 1.000 to 0.9406 at p=0.01 and 0.5647 at p=0.10. Classification AUPRC degrades from 0.4821 to 0.4678. Confirms physical noise cannot improve performance.

claims.claim_statement: Formal evaluation of the Hardware Decision Gate protocol.
claims.scientific_conclusion: Hardware Decision Gate Verdict: HARDWARE NOT JUSTIFIED. Physical QPU execution cost (~$3,217 on IonQ for N=100) is >600,000x higher than Classical ($0.000005) for a quantum model that demonstrates no simulated predictive advantage.
claims.limitations: Based on AWS Braket standard QPU pricing models.
